references.text: Abraham laughs at God's promise of a son due to his and Sarah's advanced age, which highlights the miraculous nature of Isaac's birth.
God confirms the promise that Sarah will bear a son, and that he shall be named Isaac.
God sets the time for when the promise of Isaac's birth will be fulfilled.
God's messenger predicts Isaac's birth within the coming year.
The question of whether anything is too hard for the Lord points forward to the miraculous nature of Isaac's birth.
Paul mentions Isaac's birth as a result of God's promise, contrasting it with Ishmael's birth according to the flesh.
Isaac's birth is mentioned as an example of faith, since Abraham and Sarah were too old to have children naturally.
Contrasting ages at the births of Ishmael and Isaac underscore God's supernatural fulfillment of His promise.
The combination of age at birth and total lifespan shows Abraham's long period with the promise fulfilled.
Parallel ages at birth (Abraham 100, Isaac 60) emphasize God's sovereignty over biological impossibility.
The description of Abraham as 'old' in Gen 24:1 confirms and contextualizes his age of 100 years from Gen 21:5.
Abraham's faith in God's power (Rom 4:21) gives theological meaning to the biological impossibility at age 100 (Gen 21:5).
